_provenance.notes: Marine survival rate is the percentage of juvenile salmon leaving freshwater as smolts that survive to become adults. This is the single most important determinant of adult salmon abundance, yet it is difficult to measure directly. Estimates come from coded wire tag recoveries, scale pattern analysis, and smolt-to-adult return ratios at weirs. Major decline in Chinook marine survival is the root cause of the Yukon River and West Coast Chinook crisis.
